text.p: Left-arm paceman Mike Smith completed a career-best 10 for 106 to thrust Gloucestershire to the first victory of the English county championship season on Saturday.
Smith captured six for 45 to add to his first innings tally of four for 61 as Gloucestershire beat Hampshire by six wickets on the fourth and final day at Bristol.
Gloucestershire, the only county in the 18-team championship with a win after a rain-plagued start to the campaign, are the early leaders on 32 points from second-placed Glamorgan (21).

Smith had taken two of his second innings wickets overnight when Hampshire, 87 behind, struggled to 46 for three. He continued to pose problems when they resumed, straightening the ball off a length as they subsided to 145 all out.
Needing only 59 to win, Gloucestershire were shaken when medium-fast bowler Simon Renshaw picked up four for 30 before captain Mark Alleyne and new Tasmanian signing Shaun Young guided them home.
Durham's hopes of a first championship win since 1995 were ruined by rain that brought Nottinghamshire a reprieve at Hartlepool.
Notts were 200 for six in their second innings -- just 39 ahead -- when a downpour brought the match to a premature end.
Durham, bottom of the table in 1996, are making an encouraging start to the new season under the captaincy of former Australian test batsman David Boon.
They battled into a winning position by removing Tim Robinson (69 from 171 balls) and skipper Paul Johnson (34) just before lunch.
A mixture of rain and former England batsman Bill Athey's defiance saved Sussex from defeat against Middlesex at Lord's.
Athey, unbeaten on 60 in his side's first innings of 187 all out, was fifth out for 31 when Sussex followed on 303 behind.
They had struggled to 119 for six at the finish, paceman Jamie Hewitt grabbing three wickets in 13 balls as Sussex slumped to 97 for six with 11 overs still to go.
A last-day washout saved champions Leicestershire from possible defeat against Worcestershire.
Leicestershire were 141 for four and still 47 runs short of avoiding an innings defeat when the rain came.
